one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Nutanix (fiscal year ends July 31) reported Q4 FY26 on 2026-08-26 and Q1 FY27 (quarter ends Oct 31) will be reported in late November, after 2026-10-31. Scheduled items inside the window are minor: President/CCO Tarkan Maner's departure takes effect 2026-10-02 (already disclosed 2026-09-24, CEO takes over sales), and the ~5% workforce reduction is due to be substantially complete by end of October (cost-positive, already in guidance). The company's quarter-end on Oct 31 can bring pre-announcements only in a distress case, which nothing in the filings suggests. The stock has a strong six-month uptrend (from ~$34 in April to ~$71) and buyback capacity ($728.9M remaining), a small positive tilt, offset by the stock sitting near the top of its range after a run. I therefore stay close to a symmetric lognormal spread centred at ~$70.9 (about +0.3% drift) with monthly sigma ~13% (47% annual / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY28 non-GAAP EPS ~$2.65 x 28 = $74, weight 50%), FCF-yield on FY28 FCF (~$1.02B x 21 + $2.36B cash, /292M diluted shares = $81.5, weight 25%) and an SBC-burdened DCF ($51, weight 25%); blended ~$70, close to the current price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (FY28, Aug-27 to Jul-28) non-GAAP EPS ~$2.65 x 28x

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.205B x 24.5% = $785M op income + ~$60M non-GAAP other income (FY26 GAAP other income $53M ex convert interest) x (1 - 20% long-term non-GAAP tax rate stated in release) / ~294M diluted shares (Q1 guide).

Revenue +11% to ~$3.56B (ARR growth guided to decelerate modestly from 16%; renewals cohort growing slower); margin +150bp to ~26% in line with the 260bp FY26 expansion and post-restructuring cost base; 20% tax; ~292M shares as buybacks offset SBC dilution. Company's pattern of beating initial guidance (FY26 guided $2.80-2.84B in Feb, delivered $2.85B) gives upside risk.
Current price $70.7 / FY27E $2.30 = ~31x trailing-forward; post-Q4 sell-side targets cluster $63-90 (implying ~24-34x FY28E). 28x assumes slight multiple compression as growth decelerates to ~11%.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$1.02B x 21x + $2.36B cash and investments, / 292M diluted shares (convert shares included in the count, so convert principal is not deducted)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 midpoint $900M + ~$38M nonrecurring restructuring added back, grown ~9%.
Treated as if-converted inside the ~292-294M diluted share count, consistent with company's diluted EPS method.
Current EV ~$18.4B (294M x $70.7 less $2.36B cash) / FY27 FCF guide $900M = ~20x; held near that level.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF less SBC: FY27 $510M rising to $880M by FY31; WACC 10%; terminal growth 3.5%; plus $2.36B cash; /292M shares; rolled forward 1 year

inputs_detail.derivation: Grown ~5%/yr; deducted from FCF because it is a real cost to shareholders that buybacks ($483.5M in FY26) are spent offsetting.
Guide midpoint then ~10%/yr growth, in line with ARR growth decelerating from 16% and NRR at 106%.
Equity-like cost of capital for a 47%-vol mid-cap software name with minimal net debt; terminal growth near nominal GDP.

bear.story: Server/memory shortage (32-40 week lead times) persists through FY27 and customers shrink or delay projects; NRR slides below 105% (already down from 109% to 106%), ARR growth falls toward 10% and FY27 revenue lands at low end; sales leadership churn after the CCO departure hurts execution; multiple compresses to ~20x on ~$2.35 FY28 EPS.

base.story: Company continues its pattern of conservative guidance and beats (every FY26 quarter beat; FY26 revenue ended above the Feb guide), FY27 revenue ~$3.22B, margin ~25%, FY28 EPS ~$2.65-2.70 at ~28x; buybacks keep share count flat.

bull.story: Supply chain eases in 2H FY27, VMware-by-Broadcom renewal waves plus external-storage (Dell, Everpure, NetApp) and AI offerings drive ARR re-acceleration to mid-to-high teens; FY28 EPS ~$3.00 at ~34x.

thesis_break_reason: Around $46 the stock would trade at ~17x FY28E non-GAAP EPS and ~13x EV/FCF, a level only consistent with the durable-growth thesis breaking: e.g. a guidance cut on FY27 ARR/revenue, NRR falling further from 106%, or evidence the VMware migration opportunity is being lost to Microsoft/Red Hat. The April 2026 trough ($34) came during an acute supply-chain panic before the company decoupled software purchases from hardware delivery; a return below mid-$40s without a market-wide drawdown would signal fundamental damage rather than noise.

key_uncertainties: Duration of the server CPU/DRAM shortage: management assumes elevated lead times for all of FY27 and a higher share of future-start-date orders, which delays revenue recognition.
NRR trend (109% -> 106% YoY) and the slower-growing renewals cohort.
Pace and share capture of VMware-by-Broadcom migrations versus Microsoft Azure Local and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization.
Sales execution after the CCO departure and the 5% restructuring.
Distributor concentration: top two distributors were 39% of FY26 revenue.
SBC (~$358M/yr) versus GAAP profitability; how the market values non-GAAP vs SBC-burdened cash flow.
reasoning: Primary-document lane. From the Q4 FY26 8-K (2026-08-26): revenue $2.854B (+12%), ARR $2.55B (+16%), non-GAAP op margin 23.7% (+260bp), non-GAAP EPS $2.04, FCF $841M; FY27 guide revenue $3.18-3.23B (+12%), margin 24-25%, FCF $850-950M including $33-43M restructuring (Aug 4 8-K). Filing details the recaps skip: NRR fell to 106% from 109% (10-K); top-two distributor concentration 39%; $728.9M buyback authorization left after $483.5M repurchased in FY26 at an average $51.24; AMD bought 4.14M shares at $36.26 in May; 2027 converts ($57.74 conversion) are in the money and 2029 converts convert at $85.83, both already in the ~294M diluted share count; a $1.2B valuation-allowance release inflated GAAP EPS ($5.17) and should be ignored; equipment useful lives extended to five years from FY27 (small EPS tailwind). Guidance history from the Q2 and Q3 releases shows a consistent conservative-guide/beat pattern (FY26 revenue guide $2.80-2.84B in Feb, delivered $2.85B; Q4 margin 26.2% vs 21-23% guided). The call transcript flags the main risk: server lead times elevated through FY27 and a higher share of future-start-date orders; renewal cohort growth slowing. The stock ran from a $34 April low (supply-chain panic) to ~$71, so much of the recovery is priced: at ~31x FY27E EPS and ~20x EV/FCF. Valuation blend (P/E $74, FCF yield $81.5, SBC-burdened DCF $51) gives ~$70 fair value, near spot; the base case is set slightly higher ($75) because of the beat-and-raise pattern and buybacks. Scenario mixture (bear $47/25%, base $75/50%, bull $102/25%, lognormal widths 0.22-0.30) yields a median ~$74, P(>=71) ~56%, and a distribution width roughly consistent with the stock's 47% realized vol, with a fatter left tail reflecting the supply-chain and NRR risks. Sell-side post-Q4 targets ($63-90) used only as a sanity check on the multiple. Research limited to ~10 queries; Twelve Data estimates/targets were unavailable on the plan.
